summary: Leendert A. van Daalen was an Indologist who earned his M.A. (~1958–1966) and Ph.D. (~1966–1980) at Utrecht University under Jan Gonda and Henk Bodewitz. He served as Lecturer of Sanskrit at Utrecht (1966–1992) and held a post at Leiden University (1992).

Lei Huang is a Tibetologist who studied at the Institute of Tibetan Plateau Research, Chinese Academy of Sciences in 2012. In 2022, Huang was appointed Assistant Professor at Capital Normal University.

Lei Rong, a scholar in Tibetology and other fields, earned a BSc at East China Normal University and completed an Erasmus Mundus Masters across the Universities of Oslo, Roehampton, and Charles University (2015–2017). Rong held a post at Xizang Minzu University.
Leigh Lisker was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He earned a B.A. from the University of Pennsylvania (~1937–1941), where he later served as Assistant Professor from 1948 to 1989.

Lemuel Sadoc was a scholar of philosophy and Indology who completed a Ph.D. at Goethe University Frankfurt by 1924. Sadoc served as Professor at St. Stephen's College, Delhi (1926) and taught English, French, and German at IIT (ISM) Dhanbad.

Leo Buschardt was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who earned an M.A. at the University of Copenhagen (1925–1935). He held library posts at the Royal Veterinary and Agricultural University (1943) and the Royal Danish Library (1944).

Leo Frobenius was a scholar of history and archaeology. He held posts at the Frobenius Institute (1920–1938), Goethe University Frankfurt (1932–1938), Museum der Weltkulturen (1935–1938), and the Berliner Gesellschaft für Anthropologie, Ethnologie und Urgeschichte.

Leo Joachim Frachtenberg worked in linguistics and other fields, studying at Cornell and Columbia under Franz Boas and A. V. Williams Jackson. He served as an ethnologist at the Bureau of American Ethnology (~1909–1917) and lectured at Columbia (1910–1912).

Leo M. Pruden was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at the University of Tokyo under Akira Hirakawa and Taitetsu Unno. He taught at Brown University (1970–1971), Nyingma Institute (1971), and the University of Oriental Studies (attested 1988–1991).

Leo Meyer, a linguist and Indologist, studied at Göttingen and Berlin under Theodor Benfey, Franz Bopp, and Jacob Grimm. He held positions at the University of Göttingen (1856–1865, 1898) and the University of Tartu (1865–1899).
Leo Rishi Nelson Jones is an Indology scholar who studied at the University of Hamburg and is attested there as a Wissenschaftlicher Projektmitarbeiter in 2026.

Leo Strauss was a philosopher who studied at Hamburg, Freiburg, Marburg, Columbia, and under Ernst Cassirer. His academic career included positions at Cambridge, Columbia, The New School, the University of Chicago (~1949–1968), Claremont McKenna College, and St. John's College.

Leo von Mankowski was an Indologist who studied at Leipzig, Breslau under Stenzler and Hillebrandt, and Vienna under Bühler. He founded and held posts at Jagiellonian University as Docent of Sanskrit (1894) and extraordinary Professor (1904).

Leon Cyboran, a scholar of Indology and philosophy, studied at Breslau and Warsaw, completing his Ph.D. under Eugeniusz Słuszkiewicz. He taught Sanskrit and Indian philosophy at the University of Warsaw (1965–1973) and became a professor at KUL in 1973.

Leon Hurvitz was a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology who studied at the University of Chicago and Columbia University (Ph.D.). He served as Assistant Professor at the University of Washington (~1955–1971) and Professor at the University of British Columbia (1971–1988).
Leon Sommers Swartzberg Jr. was an Indologist who earned an M.A. from Columbia University (1962–1966). In 1970, he held a post teaching anthropology at Southern Oregon University.

Leonard Bloomfield, a linguist and Indologist, studied at Harvard, Wisconsin, Chicago, Leipzig, and Göttingen. His faculty posts included Illinois Urbana-Champaign (1910–1921), Ohio State (1921–1927), the University of Chicago (1927–1940), and Yale University (1940–1949).
Leonard Blussé is a scholar in history, archaeology, and sinology. He studied at Leiden University from ~1964 to 1972 and later held a post there from 1998 to 2011.

Leonard C. D. C. Priestley is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology who studied under F. E. L. Priestley and doctoral supervisor Anthony Kennedy Warder. He held a post at the University of Toronto, attested in 1991.
Leonard John Sedgwick was a scholar in Indology and other fields. He completed his B.A. studies at Pembroke College, University of Cambridge, between ~1902 and 1905.
